concerns.text: FR-001 mandates at least 50 plant species with paired data, but the Assumptions section states the analysis will be restricted to the available species count if fewer than 50 are found, effectively allowing a fallback that violates the mandatory requirement.

FR-003 requires automatically identifying 3‑5 metabolite classes with a statistically significant negative correlation (p < 0.05), while FR-006 mandates applying a multiple‑comparison correction to all p‑values. The identification criterion should reference the corrected p‑values (q < 0.05) to remain consistent.

SC-001 states “measured against the target of an appropriate sample size of species” without specifying a concrete numeric target, making the criterion unmeasurable. Testability requires a definite threshold (e.g., ≥ 50 paired species).
The phrase “processes data in batches of a moderate number of species” is vague; the batch size must be explicitly defined (e.g., batches of ≤ 20 species) to allow deterministic testing.

Runtime limit is expressed as “must not exceed 6 hours on the CI runner,” but the CI environment can vary. Clarify the exact runner configuration (CPU, RAM) that defines the benchmark, or tie the limit to a reproducible hardware profile.

FR-003 validates the identification of metabolite classes by requiring a statistically significant negative correlation (p < 0.05) *derived from the same correlation analysis* that produces the metric. The validation target (significant negative correlation) is not independent of the predictor; it is a tautological check that the correlation exists, providing no external ground‑truth to confirm that the identified classes are true biomarkers.

SC-002 uses the model’s own R² (> 0.3) on the same 80/20 split (with cross‑validation) as the sole evidence of biomarker utility. This is a circular validation because predictive performance is assessed on data that informed model training, without an independent test set or external validation dataset.

FR-001 mandates ≥ 50 plant species with paired metabolomics‑herbivory data, yet the number of predictors (potentially many individual metabolites within each class) is not bounded. If the feature set exceeds the sample size, the multiple linear regression will be under‑determined, violating standard statistical practice for regression modeling.

responses.response: Made FR-001 and the Assumptions consistent by requiring a hard minimum of 50 paired species; the system aborts with a clear error if insufficient data are available.
responses.what_changed: Updated FR-001 wording and added abort clause; revised Assumptions to state the 50‑species minimum is mandatory.

responses.response: Aligned FR-003 with the multiple‑comparison correction by referencing the corrected q‑value threshold.
responses.what_changed: Changed FR-003 to require q < 0.05 after correction; updated SC-003 to match.

responses.response: Provided a concrete numeric target for SC-001.
responses.what_changed: SC-001 now specifies “≥ 50 paired plant species”.

responses.response: Specified exact batch size in User Story 1 Acceptance Scenario 3.
responses.what_changed: Replaced vague “moderate number of species” with “batches of ≤ 20 species”.

responses.response: Clarified the CI runner hardware profile that defines the 6‑hour runtime limit.
responses.what_changed: SC-005 now ties the limit to the standard GitHub Actions runner (2 vCPU, 7 GB RAM, Ubuntu‑latest).

responses.response: Added an external validation step against a curated literature list of known defense metabolites.
responses.what_changed: Introduced new FR-009 (external validation) and referenced it from US‑2; updated assumptions to note the external list source.

responses.response: Added an independent test‑set evaluation requirement and modified SC-002 accordingly.
responses.what_changed: Created FR-010 (independent validation set) and changed SC-002 to require R² > 0.3 on that independent set.

responses.response: Bound the predictor dimensionality to avoid under‑determined regression models.
responses.what_changed: Added FR-011 limiting predictors to a maximum of 20 (≤ 5 per metabolite class) selected by variance, and noted this in the assumptions.

new_concerns.text: FR-011 performs variance‑based feature selection on the full dataset before any train‑test split or cross‑validation. Selecting predictors on the entire data can leak information from the validation set into the model, inflating performance metrics (R²). The specification should require that feature selection be confined to the training folds (e.g., within each cross‑validation split) to avoid data‑leakage.
